key_reasoning.reason: Base XL: the change spans the analytics CLI command (index.ts: --export/-o/--open resolution and format inference), the cost subsystem (cost-enricher, cost types), the report subsystem (report-generator, payload-builder, session-report, report types, HTML client app.js, new output-target resolver), the OTEL path (otel-loader, otel-pricing), shared pricing utilities (new price-resolution.ts resolver, pricing.ts, model-normalizer.ts, pricing.json), the Claude statusline plugin and Codex rollout correlation. New abstractions: price-resolution (a single model-id to price-key resolver shared by the report and the bundled statusline) and output-target. Bumped to XXL because it touches core shared utilities consumed across agents.

Diffstat reports 43 files changed (+2928/-715): about 22 source/data/doc files and 21 unit and integration test files across src/cli/commands/analytics (and its cost/ and report/ subdirs), src/utils, src/agents/plugins/claude, src/agents/plugins/codex, tests/integration, tests/helpers and docs. New files include price-resolution.ts, output-target.ts and several new test suites. This is well past the 16+ threshold, so XXL.

4 layers: UI (HTML report client app.js and terminal formatter), API/CLI surface (analytics command options and export semantics), Service (cost enrichment, pricing resolution, OTEL pricing), and External/agent integration (Claude statusline and Codex native-log correlation). Persistence is limited to report file output and reading session metadata, with no schema change or migration, so the score stays at L.

Established patterns cover most of the work: the pricing table, the enricher with injected deps and the report generator already existed, and the resolver is pure and side-effect free with deterministic ordered matching (exact, snapshot-stripped, Claude family reorder). There are no security, auth or persistence-migration implications. Edge cases (invalid formats, directory vs file -o targets, snapshot suffixes) are covered by existing Vitest table-style test templates, so no auto-bump applies. The main risk is keeping costs consistent between the statusline and the report, which the reconciliation integration tests address. Stays M.
